# H020 — The matched decoy set yields fewer biallelic candidates per gene than the target set.

**Status:** refuted  |  **Confidence:** 0.07  |  **Revisions:** 3

## The claim

The matched decoy set yields fewer biallelic candidates per gene than the target set.

**Prediction if true.** Running every rule of steps 2-3 identically over results.it2_decoys gives a lower per-gene rate of biallelic candidates than over results.it2_targets — the read route's empirical false-lead rate.

**What would refute it.** As many or more per gene: the read route has no discriminating power of its own and enters the step-6 fusion at reduced weight.

## Weighing

```
prior 0.50  (log-odds +0.000)
  +0.700  supports 0.35 — Target genes yield a biallelic candidate at 4/396 against the decoys' 2/396 — twice the rate — and restricting to genes above half the median bait density does not change it (4/391 vs 2/380).   -> 0.668
  +0.000  neutral 0.40 — With four events against two the comparison has almost no power: Fisher one-sided p = 0.343, so a true twofold difference and no difference at all are both consistent with this result.   -> 0.668
  -1.000  refutes 0.50 — Without the rarity and consequence filter the decoys yield MORE biallelic genes per gene than the targets (0.573 vs 0.509 core), so the gene selection alone carries no discriminating power — the filter does.   -> 0.426
  -1.300  refutes 0.65 — Scoring every read-derived allele rather than only the vendor-reported ones, targets and decoys yield the same per-gene rate of biallelic candidates: 10 of 396 against 10 of 396, Fisher one-sided p = 0.589; on the pre-registered reachable-gene view the decoys are marginally ahead at 9 of 380 against 9 of 391.   -> 0.168
  -1.000  refutes 0.50 — The twofold difference reported earlier was an artefact of the scoring join reading only annotations built from the delivered callset, which restricted the enumeration to alleles the vendor had already found and favoured the target set more than the decoy set.   -> 0.069
suggested confidence 0.07 (1 supporting, 3 refuting, 1 neutral)
```

The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior: the strengths are human judgments, and rows drawn from the same underlying data are not independent the way the sum treats them.

## History

| Rev | Status | Confidence | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | proposed | — | — |
| 2 | supported | 0.45 | Supported in direction and not in strength. Targets 4/396 against decoys 2/396, unchanged when restricted to reachable genes as entry 085 pre-registered (4/391 vs 2/380) — so the bait-density imbalance between the two sets did not create the difference. But four events against two is Fisher p = 0.343 one-sided: this design cannot distinguish a twofold effect from none, and confidence is set at 0.45 to say so rather than at the heuristic's number. The finding that matters more than the verdict is the counterfactual: run the same enumeration WITHOUT the rarity and consequence filter and the decoys score higher than the targets. The discriminating power is in the filter, not in the symptom-derived gene list, and any later step that quotes a target-versus-decoy rate has to say which version it means. |
| 3 | refuted | 0.07 | Refuted on its own pre-registered condition. H020 said the decoy set would yield FEWER biallelic candidates per gene and named 'as many or more' as the refutation; with every read-derived allele scored rather than only the ones the delivered callset had already reported, the two sets are exactly equal at 10 of 396 (Fisher one-sided p = 0.589) and on the pre-registered reachable-gene view the decoys are marginally ahead (9/380 against 9/391). The earlier twofold difference came from a scoring join that could only see vendor-reported alleles, which is the circle a blind second-caller route exists to avoid. The consequence was written into the claim before it was tested and stands: the read route has no discriminating power of its own and enters the step-6 fusion at reduced weight. The confidence is low rather than zero because the design is still underpowered - 10 events against 10 cannot exclude a small true effect any more than it can show one - and because the 1,199 newly scored alleles are unvalidated until step 3 checks them. |
